e-8054.knowledge_point: Reducing a 4x4 Determinant to a 3x3 Determinant Using Row Operations
e-8054.problem:
$$
|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & 5 & -7 \\ 4 & -2 & 4 & -5 \\ -3 & 3 & -3 & -4\end{aligned}|
$$

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Find a $3\times 3$ determinant that has the same value.

*Hint: Use elementary row operations to make the entries below $a_{11}$ equal to zero.*
e-8054.worked_solution:
Let's make entries below $a_{11}=1$ equal to zero using elementary row operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (or column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & 5 & -7 \\ 4 & -2 & 4 & -5 \\ -3 & 3 & -3 & -4\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-4){R}_{1} \\ {R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+3{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & -5 & -1 & -9 \\ 0 & -10 & -8 & -9 \\ 0 & 9 & 6 & -1\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $1$st column, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & -5 & -1 & -9 \\ 0 & -10 & -8 & -9 \\ 0 & 9 & 6 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot (-1)^{1+1}|\begin{aligned}-5 & -1 & -9 \\ -10 & -8 & -9 \\ 9 & 6 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-5 & -1 & -9 \\ -10 & -8 & -9 \\ 9 & 6 & -1\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

e-8060.knowledge_point: Reducing a 4x4 Determinant to a 3x3 Determinant Using Column Operations
e-8060.problem:
$$
|\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 2 & 2 \\ -1 & 2 & 1 & -3 \\ 2 & -2 & -2 & 4 \\ -4 & -4 & 3 & 2\end{aligned}|
$$

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Find a $3\times 3$ determinant that has the same value.

*Hint: Use elementary column operations to make the entries to the left and to the right of $a_{23}$ equal to zero.*
e-8060.worked_solution:
Let's make entries to the left and to the right of $a_{23}=1$ equal to zero using elementary column operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (or column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 2 & 2 \\ -1 & 2 & 1 & -3 \\ 2 & -2 & -2 & 4 \\ -4 & -4 & 3 & 2\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}+{C}_{3} \\ {C}_{2}:={C}_{2}+(-2){C}_{3} \\ {C}_{4}:={C}_{4}+3{C}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}4 & -1 & 2 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & -2 & -2 \\ -1 & -10 & 3 & 11\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $2$nd row, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}4 & -1 & 2 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & -2 & -2 \\ -1 & -10 & 3 & 11\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot (-1)^{2+3}|\begin{aligned}4 & -1 & 8 \\ 0 & 2 & -2 \\ -1 & -10 & 11\end{aligned}| \\  & =-|\begin{aligned}4 & -1 & 8 \\ 0 & 2 & -2 \\ -1 & -10 & 11\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

e-8005.knowledge_point: Computing 4x4 Determinants Using Row and Column Operations
e-8005.problem:
Calculate the value of 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14058571/assets/9cb26049b5e3d06f9ef9e07ce617042166330b1eddb84063d7970799ebf6d8e5.png)

*Hint: Use elementary column operations to make the entries to the right of $a_{31}$ equal to zero. You should be able to reduce the given $4 \times 4$ determinant to a $3 \times 3$ determinant.*
e-8005.worked_solution:
Using elementary column operations, let's make entries to the right of $a_{31}=1$ equal to zero.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (or column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 3 & 2 \\ 2 & -4 & -2 & 6 \\ 1 & -2 & -3 & 3 \\ -3 & 3 & 4 & 2\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{2}:={C}_{2}+2{C}_{1} \\ {C}_{3}:={C}_{3}+3{C}_{1} \\ {C}_{4}:={C}_{4}+(-3){C}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 6 & -1 \\ 2 & 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -3 & -3 & -5 & 11\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $3$rd row, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 6 & -1 \\ 2 & 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -3 & -3 & -5 & 11\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot (-1)^{3+1}|\begin{aligned}1 & 6 & -1 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ -3 & -5 & 11\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 6 & -1 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ -3 & -5 & 11\end{aligned}| \\  & =4\cdot (-1)^{2+2}|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -3 & 11\end{aligned}| \\  & =4(11-3) \\  & =32.\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Apply R2 ← R2 + 3R1, R3 ← R3 − R1, and R4 ← R4 + 2R1. These preserve the determinant and make column 2 equal to (−1,0,0,0). Expanding along that column gives the minor in option d, since (−1)(−1)^(1+2)=1.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
$$
|\begin{aligned}3 & -1 & 4 & 3 \\ 2 & 3 & 5 & 2 \\ -3 & -1 & 3 & 2 \\ 5 & 2 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}|
$$

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

*Hint: Use elementary row operations to make the entries below ${a}_{12}$ equal to zero.*
after.worked_solution:
Let's make entries below ${a}_{12}=-1$ equal to zero using elementary row operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}3 & -1 & 4 & 3 \\ 2 & 3 & 5 & 2 \\ -3 & -1 & 3 & 2 \\ 5 & 2 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{1} \\ {R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+2{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}3 & -1 & 4 & 3 \\ 11 & 0 & 17 & 11 \\ -6 & 0 & -1 & -1 \\ 11 & 0 & 7 & 7\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $2$nd column, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}3 & -1 & 4 & 3 \\ 11 & 0 & 17 & 11 \\ -6 & 0 & -1 & -1 \\ 11 & 0 & 7 & 7\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-1)\cdot (-1)^{1+2}|\begin{aligned}11 & 17 & 11 \\ -6 & -1 & -1 \\ 11 & 7 & 7\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}11 & 17 & 11 \\ -6 & -1 & -1 \\ 11 & 7 & 7\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the above 4×4 determinant. Which of the following 3×3 determinants has the same value?

Hint: Use elementary row operations to make the entries below a12 equal to zero.

a
|111711−6−111−1110|

|343−3325−11|

EXPLANATION

Let's make entries below a12=−1 equal to zero using elementary row operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

=|3−1432352−3−13252−11|R2:=R2+3R1R3:=R3+(−1)R1R4:=R4+2R1=|3−1431101711−60−1−111077|.

Expanding the result along the 2nd column, we get

=|3−1431101711−60−1−111077|=(−1)⋅(−1)1+2|111711−6−1−11177|=|111711−6−1−11177|.

verification.explanation: The revealed solution confirms d. The determinant-preserving operations R2 ← R2 + 3R1, R3 ← R3 − R1, and R4 ← R4 + 2R1 zero the entries below −1 in column 2. Cofactor expansion gives option d because (−1)(−1)^(1+2)=1. The incorrect feedback concerns the deliberately submitted option a.

content.knowledge_point: Reducing a 4x4 Determinant to a 3x3 Determinant Using Row Operations
content.problem:
$$
|\begin{aligned}3 & -1 & 4 & 3 \\ 2 & 3 & 5 & 2 \\ -3 & -1 & 3 & 2 \\ 5 & 2 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}|
$$

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

*Hint: Use elementary row operations to make the entries below ${a}_{12}$ equal to zero.*
content.worked_solution:
Let's make entries below ${a}_{12}=-1$ equal to zero using elementary row operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}3 & -1 & 4 & 3 \\ 2 & 3 & 5 & 2 \\ -3 & -1 & 3 & 2 \\ 5 & 2 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{1} \\ {R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+2{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}3 & -1 & 4 & 3 \\ 11 & 0 & 17 & 11 \\ -6 & 0 & -1 & -1 \\ 11 & 0 & 7 & 7\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $2$nd column, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}3 & -1 & 4 & 3 \\ 11 & 0 & 17 & 11 \\ -6 & 0 & -1 & -1 \\ 11 & 0 & 7 & 7\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-1)\cdot (-1)^{1+2}|\begin{aligned}11 & 17 & 11 \\ -6 & -1 & -1 \\ 11 & 7 & 7\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}11 & 17 & 11 \\ -6 & -1 & -1 \\ 11 & 7 & 7\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Apply R1 ← R1 + 2R3, R2 ← R2 − R3, and R4 ← R4 + 2R3. These preserve the determinant and give rows (−5,5,2,0), (10,−7,6,0), (−2,4,−1,3), and (−9,6,−1,0). Expanding along column 4 yields 3(−1)^(3+4)=−3 times the minor displayed in option c.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
$$
|\begin{aligned}-1 & -3 & 4 & -6 \\ 8 & -3 & 5 & 3 \\ -2 & 4 & -1 & 3 \\ -5 & -2 & 1 & -6\end{aligned}|
$$

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

*Hint: Use elementary row operations to make the entries above and below ${a}_{34}$ equal to zero.*
after.worked_solution:
Let's make entries above and below ${a}_{34}=3$ equal to zero using elementary row operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}-1 & -3 & 4 & -6 \\ 8 & -3 & 5 & 3 \\ -2 & 4 & -1 & 3 \\ -5 & -2 & 1 & -6\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+2{R}_{3} \\ {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-{R}_{3} \\ {R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+2{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-5 & 5 & 2 & 0 \\ 10 & -7 & 6 & 0 \\ -2 & 4 & -1 & 3 \\ -9 & 6 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $4$th column, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}-5 & 5 & 2 & 0 \\ 10 & -7 & 6 & 0 \\ -2 & 4 & -1 & 3 \\ -9 & 6 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =3\cdot (-1)^{3+4}|\begin{aligned}-5 & 5 & 2 \\ 10 & -7 & 6 \\ -9 & 6 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =-3|\begin{aligned}-5 & 5 & 2 \\ 10 & -7 & 6 \\ -9 & 6 & -1\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the above 4×4 determinant. Which of the following 3×3 determinants has the same value?

Hint: Use elementary row operations to make the entries above and below a34 equal to zero.

a
−3|−55515−76−961|

−3|−25210−73−6−6−1|

−3|−55210−76−96−1|

−3|−57210−16−93−1|
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Let's make entries above and below a34=3 equal to zero using elementary row operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

=|−1−34−68−353−24−13−5−21−6|R1:=R1+2R3R2:=R2−R3R4:=R4+2R3=|−552010−760−24−13−96−10|.

Expanding the result along the 4th column, we get

=|−552010−760−24−13−96−10|=3⋅(−1)3+4|−55210−76−96−1|=−3|−55210−76−96−1|.

content.knowledge_point: Reducing a 4x4 Determinant to a 3x3 Determinant Using Row Operations
content.problem:
$$
|\begin{aligned}-1 & -3 & 4 & -6 \\ 8 & -3 & 5 & 3 \\ -2 & 4 & -1 & 3 \\ -5 & -2 & 1 & -6\end{aligned}|
$$

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

*Hint: Use elementary row operations to make the entries above and below ${a}_{34}$ equal to zero.*
content.worked_solution:
Let's make entries above and below ${a}_{34}=3$ equal to zero using elementary row operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}-1 & -3 & 4 & -6 \\ 8 & -3 & 5 & 3 \\ -2 & 4 & -1 & 3 \\ -5 & -2 & 1 & -6\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+2{R}_{3} \\ {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-{R}_{3} \\ {R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+2{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-5 & 5 & 2 & 0 \\ 10 & -7 & 6 & 0 \\ -2 & 4 & -1 & 3 \\ -9 & 6 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $4$th column, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}-5 & 5 & 2 & 0 \\ 10 & -7 & 6 & 0 \\ -2 & 4 & -1 & 3 \\ -9 & 6 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =3\cdot (-1)^{3+4}|\begin{aligned}-5 & 5 & 2 \\ 10 & -7 & 6 \\ -9 & 6 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =-3|\begin{aligned}-5 & 5 & 2 \\ 10 & -7 & 6 \\ -9 & 6 & -1\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

|1−2−33212−3343−2−1−1−44|

Consider the above 4×4 determinant. Which of the following 3×3 determinants has the same value?

Hint: Use elementary row operations to make the entries above and below a22 equal to zero.

a
|22−3−510−511−2|
b
|51−3−5−51101−2|
c
|1−3322−333−2|
d
|22−333−2−1−44|
e
|51−3−5−5101−21|
Submit

decision.explanation: Apply R1 ← R1 + 2R2, R3 ← R3 − 4R2, and R4 ← R4 + R2. These preserve the determinant and make column 2 equal to (0,1,0,0). Deleting row 2 and column 2 gives rows (5,1,−3), (−5,−5,10), and (1,−2,1). The cofactor factor is 1·(−1)^(2+2)=1, so option e has the same value.

after.name: Question 3
after.problem:
$$
|\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -3 & 3 \\ 2 & 1 & 2 & -3 \\ 3 & 4 & 3 & -2 \\ -1 & -1 & -4 & 4\end{aligned}|
$$

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

*Hint: Use elementary row operations to make the entries above and below ${a}_{22}$ equal to zero.*
after.worked_solution:
Let's make entries above and below ${a}_{22}=1$ equal to zero using elementary row operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -3 & 3 \\ 2 & 1 & 2 & -3 \\ 3 & 4 & 3 & -2 \\ -1 & -1 & -4 & 4\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+2{R}_{2} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-4){R}_{2} \\ {R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 1 & -3 \\ 2 & 1 & 2 & -3 \\ -5 & 0 & -5 & 10 \\ 1 & 0 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $2$nd column, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 1 & -3 \\ 2 & 1 & 2 & -3 \\ -5 & 0 & -5 & 10 \\ 1 & 0 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot (-1)^{2+2}|\begin{aligned}5 & 1 & -3 \\ -5 & -5 & 10 \\ 1 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}5 & 1 & -3 \\ -5 & -5 & 10 \\ 1 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Hint: Use elementary row operations to make the entries above and below a22 equal to zero.

a
|22−3−510−511−2|

|51−3−5−51101−2|

EXPLANATION

Let's make entries above and below a22=1 equal to zero using elementary row operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

=|1−2−33212−3343−2−1−1−44|R1:=R1+2R2R3:=R3+(−4)R2R4:=R4+R2=|501−3212−3−50−51010−21|.

Expanding the result along the 2nd column, we get

=|501−3212−3−50−51010−21|=1⋅(−1)2+2|51−3−5−5101−21|=|51−3−5−5101−21|.

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms option e. The determinant-preserving operations R1 ← R1 + 2R2, R3 ← R3 − 4R2, and R4 ← R4 + R2 make column 2 equal to (0,1,0,0). Expanding along that column gives the displayed minor in e with factor 1·(−1)^(2+2)=1. The incorrect feedback applies to the deliberately submitted option d.

content.knowledge_point: Reducing a 4x4 Determinant to a 3x3 Determinant Using Row Operations
content.problem:
$$
|\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -3 & 3 \\ 2 & 1 & 2 & -3 \\ 3 & 4 & 3 & -2 \\ -1 & -1 & -4 & 4\end{aligned}|
$$

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

*Hint: Use elementary row operations to make the entries above and below ${a}_{22}$ equal to zero.*
content.worked_solution:
Let's make entries above and below ${a}_{22}=1$ equal to zero using elementary row operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -3 & 3 \\ 2 & 1 & 2 & -3 \\ 3 & 4 & 3 & -2 \\ -1 & -1 & -4 & 4\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+2{R}_{2} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-4){R}_{2} \\ {R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 1 & -3 \\ 2 & 1 & 2 & -3 \\ -5 & 0 & -5 & 10 \\ 1 & 0 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $2$nd column, we get

$$

Question 4
?

|2−2−33−3−4−212−723−613−2−3|

Consider the above 4×4 determinant. Which of the following 3×3 determinants has the same value?

Hint: Use elementary row operations to make the entries below a14 equal to zero.

a
−|−2−33−4−21223−6|
b
−12|2−2−3−72313−2|
c
−3|−11410−3−2513−3|
d
−3|2−23−3−412−72−6|
e
−3|−11410−3−2−331−5|
Submit

decision.explanation: Apply R2 ← R2 − 4R1, R3 ← R3 + 2R1, and R4 ← R4 + R1. These preserve the determinant and zero the entries below 3 in column 4. The remaining minor has rows (−11,4,10), (−3,−2,−3), and (3,1,−5). Expanding along column 4 multiplies it by 3(−1)^(1+4)=−3, giving option e.

after.name: Question 4
after.problem:
$$
|\begin{aligned}2 & -2 & -3 & 3 \\ -3 & -4 & -2 & 12 \\ -7 & 2 & 3 & -6 \\ 1 & 3 & -2 & -3\end{aligned}|
$$

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

*Hint: Use elementary row operations to make the entries below ${a}_{14}$ equal to zero.*
after.worked_solution:
Let's make entries below ${a}_{14}=3$ equal to zero using elementary row operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}2 & -2 & -3 & 3 \\ -3 & -4 & -2 & 12 \\ -7 & 2 & 3 & -6 \\ 1 & 3 & -2 & -3\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-4){R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+2{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}2 & -2 & -3 & 3 \\ -11 & 4 & 10 & 0 \\ -3 & -2 & -3 & 0 \\ 3 & 1 & -5 & 0\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $4$th column, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}2 & -2 & -3 & 3 \\ -11 & 4 & 10 & 0 \\ -3 & -2 & -3 & 0 \\ 3 & 1 & -5 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =3\cdot (-1)^{1+4}|\begin{aligned}-11 & 4 & 10 \\ -3 & -2 & -3 \\ 3 & 1 & -5\end{aligned}| \\  & =-3|\begin{aligned}-11 & 4 & 10 \\ -3 & -2 & -3 \\ 3 & 1 & -5\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 4
?

|2−2−33−3−4−212−723−613−2−3|

Consider the above 4×4 determinant. Which of the following 3×3 determinants has the same value?

Hint: Use elementary row operations to make the entries below a14 equal to zero.

a
−|−2−33−4−21223−6|
b
−12|2−2−3−72313−2|
c
−3|−11410−3−2513−3|
d
−3|2−23−3−412−72−6|
e
−3|−11410−3−2−331−5|
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Let's make entries below a14=3 equal to zero using elementary row operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

=|2−2−33−3−4−212−723−613−2−3|R2:=R2+(−4)R1R3:=R3+2R1R4:=R4+R1=|2−2−33−114100−3−2−3031−50|.

Expanding the result along the 4th column, we get

=|2−2−33−114100−3−2−3031−50|=3⋅(−1)1+4|−11410−3−2−331−5|=−3|−11410−3−2−331−5|.

content.knowledge_point: Reducing a 4x4 Determinant to a 3x3 Determinant Using Row Operations
content.problem:
$$
|\begin{aligned}2 & -2 & -3 & 3 \\ -3 & -4 & -2 & 12 \\ -7 & 2 & 3 & -6 \\ 1 & 3 & -2 & -3\end{aligned}|
$$

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

*Hint: Use elementary row operations to make the entries below ${a}_{14}$ equal to zero.*
content.worked_solution:
Let's make entries below ${a}_{14}=3$ equal to zero using elementary row operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}2 & -2 & -3 & 3 \\ -3 & -4 & -2 & 12 \\ -7 & 2 & 3 & -6 \\ 1 & 3 & -2 & -3\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-4){R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+2{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}2 & -2 & -3 & 3 \\ -11 & 4 & 10 & 0 \\ -3 & -2 & -3 & 0 \\ 3 & 1 & -5 & 0\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $4$th column, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}2 & -2 & -3 & 3 \\ -11 & 4 & 10 & 0 \\ -3 & -2 & -3 & 0 \\ 3 & 1 & -5 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =3\cdot (-1)^{1+4}|\begin{aligned}-11 & 4 & 10 \\ -3 & -2 & -3 \\ 3 & 1 & -5\end{aligned}| \\  & =-3|\begin{aligned}-11 & 4 & 10 \\ -3 & -2 & -3 \\ 3 & 1 & -5\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Apply R1 ← R1 + 2R2, R3 ← R3 + 4R2, and R4 ← R4 + R2. These preserve the determinant and zero all entries in column 3 except −2 in row 2. Deleting row 2 and column 3 gives rows (8,4,13), (11,9,26), and (6,4,10). The cofactor factor is (−2)(−1)^(2+3)=2, giving option c.

after.name: Question 5
after.problem:
$$
|\begin{aligned}4 & 2 & 4 & 3 \\ 2 & 1 & -2 & 5 \\ 3 & 5 & 8 & 6 \\ 4 & 3 & 2 & 5\end{aligned}|
$$

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

*Hint: Use elementary row operations to make the entries above and below ${a}_{23}$ equal to zero.*
after.worked_solution:
Let's make entries above and below ${a}_{23}=-2$ equal to zero using elementary row operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}4 & 2 & 4 & 3 \\ 2 & 1 & -2 & 5 \\ 3 & 5 & 8 & 6 \\ 4 & 3 & 2 & 5\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+2{R}_{2} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+4{R}_{2} \\ {R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}8 & 4 & 0 & 13 \\ 2 & 1 & -2 & 5 \\ 11 & 9 & 0 & 26 \\ 6 & 4 & 0 & 10\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $3$rd column, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}8 & 4 & 0 & 13 \\ 2 & 1 & -2 & 5 \\ 11 & 9 & 0 & 26 \\ 6 & 4 & 0 & 10\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-2)\cdot (-1)^{2+3}|\begin{aligned}8 & 4 & 13 \\ 11 & 9 & 26 \\ 6 & 4 & 10\end{aligned}| \\  & =2|\begin{aligned}8 & 4 & 13 \\ 11 & 9 & 26 \\ 6 & 4 & 10\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the above 4×4 determinant. Which of the following 3×3 determinants has the same value?

Hint: Use elementary row operations to make the entries above and below a23 equal to zero.

a
2|215356435|
b
2|841311964816|
c
2|8413119266410|
d
2|423215435|
e
2|423215356|
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Let's make entries above and below a23=−2 equal to zero using elementary row operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

=|424321−2535864325|R1:=R1+2R2R3:=R3+4R2R4:=R4+R2=|8401321−2511902664010|

Expanding the result along the 3rd column, we get

=|8401321−2511902664010|=(−2)⋅(−1)2+3|8413119266410|=2|8413119266410|.

content.knowledge_point: Reducing a 4x4 Determinant to a 3x3 Determinant Using Row Operations
content.problem:
$$
|\begin{aligned}4 & 2 & 4 & 3 \\ 2 & 1 & -2 & 5 \\ 3 & 5 & 8 & 6 \\ 4 & 3 & 2 & 5\end{aligned}|
$$

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

*Hint: Use elementary row operations to make the entries above and below ${a}_{23}$ equal to zero.*
content.worked_solution:
Let's make entries above and below ${a}_{23}=-2$ equal to zero using elementary row operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}4 & 2 & 4 & 3 \\ 2 & 1 & -2 & 5 \\ 3 & 5 & 8 & 6 \\ 4 & 3 & 2 & 5\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+2{R}_{2} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+4{R}_{2} \\ {R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}8 & 4 & 0 & 13 \\ 2 & 1 & -2 & 5 \\ 11 & 9 & 0 & 26 \\ 6 & 4 & 0 & 10\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $3$rd column, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}8 & 4 & 0 & 13 \\ 2 & 1 & -2 & 5 \\ 11 & 9 & 0 & 26 \\ 6 & 4 & 0 & 10\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-2)\cdot (-1)^{2+3}|\begin{aligned}8 & 4 & 13 \\ 11 & 9 & 26 \\ 6 & 4 & 10\end{aligned}| \\  & =2|\begin{aligned}8 & 4 & 13 \\ 11 & 9 & 26 \\ 6 & 4 & 10\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Apply C1 ← C1 + 2C3, C2 ← C2 − 4C3, and C4 ← C4 − 3C3. These preserve the determinant and make row 4 equal to (0,0,−1,0). Deleting row 4 and column 3 gives rows (14,−20,−21), (17,−31,−23), and (3,2,6). The cofactor factor is (−1)(−1)^(4+3)=1, giving option c.

after.name: Question 6
after.problem:
$$
|\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & 6 & -3 \\ 3 & -3 & 7 & -2 \\ 5 & -2 & -1 & 3 \\ 2 & -4 & -1 & -3\end{aligned}|
$$

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

*Hint: Use elementary column operations to make the entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{43}$ equal to zero.*
after.worked_solution:
Let's make entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{43}=-1$ equal to zero using elementary column operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & 6 & -3 \\ 3 & -3 & 7 & -2 \\ 5 & -2 & -1 & 3 \\ 2 & -4 & -1 & -3\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}+2{C}_{3} \\ {C}_{2}:={C}_{2}+(-4){C}_{3} \\ {C}_{4}:={C}_{4}+(-3){C}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}14 & -20 & 6 & -21 \\ 17 & -31 & 7 & -23 \\ 3 & 2 & -1 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $4$th row, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}14 & -20 & 6 & -21 \\ 17 & -31 & 7 & -23 \\ 3 & 2 & -1 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-1)\cdot (-1)^{4+3}|\begin{aligned}14 & -20 & -21 \\ 17 & -31 & -23 \\ 3 & 2 & 6\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}14 & -20 & -21 \\ 17 & -31 & -23 \\ 3 & 2 & 6\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the above 4×4 determinant. Which of the following 3×3 determinants has the same value?

Hint: Use elementary column operations to make the entries to the left and to the right of a43 equal to zero.

a
|24−33−3−25−23|
b
|46−3−37−2−2−13|

Correct
EXPLANATION

Let's make entries to the left and to the right of a43=−1 equal to zero using elementary column operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

=|246−33−37−25−2−132−4−1−3|C1:=C1+2C3C2:=C2+(−4)C3C4:=C4+(−3)C3=|14−206−2117−317−2332−1600−10|.

Expanding the result along the 4th row, we get

=|14−206−2117−317−2332−1600−10|=(−1)⋅(−1)4+3|14−20−2117−31−23326|=|14−20−2117−31−23326|.

content.knowledge_point: Reducing a 4x4 Determinant to a 3x3 Determinant Using Column Operations
content.problem:
$$
|\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & 6 & -3 \\ 3 & -3 & 7 & -2 \\ 5 & -2 & -1 & 3 \\ 2 & -4 & -1 & -3\end{aligned}|
$$

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

*Hint: Use elementary column operations to make the entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{43}$ equal to zero.*
content.worked_solution:
Let's make entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{43}=-1$ equal to zero using elementary column operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & 6 & -3 \\ 3 & -3 & 7 & -2 \\ 5 & -2 & -1 & 3 \\ 2 & -4 & -1 & -3\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}+2{C}_{3} \\ {C}_{2}:={C}_{2}+(-4){C}_{3} \\ {C}_{4}:={C}_{4}+(-3){C}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}14 & -20 & 6 & -21 \\ 17 & -31 & 7 & -23 \\ 3 & 2 & -1 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $4$th row, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}14 & -20 & 6 & -21 \\ 17 & -31 & 7 & -23 \\ 3 & 2 & -1 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-1)\cdot (-1)^{4+3}|\begin{aligned}14 & -20 & -21 \\ 17 & -31 & -23 \\ 3 & 2 & 6\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}14 & -20 & -21 \\ 17 & -31 & -23 \\ 3 & 2 & 6\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Apply C1 ← C1 + C2, C3 ← C3 − C2, and C4 ← C4 + 3C2. These preserve the determinant and make row 3 equal to (0,2,0,0). Deleting row 3 and column 2 gives rows (−1,−5,4), (−10,−5,6), and (3,3,−4). The cofactor factor is 2(−1)^(3+2)=−2, giving option d.

after.name: Question 7
after.problem:
$$
|\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -7 & 10 \\ -9 & -1 & -6 & 9 \\ -2 & 2 & 2 & -6 \\ 2 & 1 & 4 & -7\end{aligned}|
$$

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

*Hint: Use elementary column operations to make the entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{32}$ equal to zero.*
after.worked_solution:
Let's make entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{32}=2$ equal to zero using elementary column operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -7 & 10 \\ -9 & -1 & -6 & 9 \\ -2 & 2 & 2 & -6 \\ 2 & 1 & 4 & -7\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}+{C}_{2} \\ {C}_{3}:={C}_{3}+(-1){C}_{2} \\ {C}_{4}:={C}_{4}+3{C}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 & -5 & 4 \\ -10 & -1 & -5 & 6 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & 1 & 3 & -4\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $3$rd row, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 & -5 & 4 \\ -10 & -1 & -5 & 6 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & 1 & 3 & -4\end{aligned}| \\  & =2\cdot (-1)^{3+2}|\begin{aligned}-1 & -5 & 4 \\ -10 & -5 & 6 \\ 3 & 3 & -4\end{aligned}| \\  & =-2|\begin{aligned}-1 & -5 & 4 \\ -10 & -5 & 6 \\ 3 & 3 & -4\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Reducing a 4x4 Determinant to a 3x3 Determinant Using Column Operations
content.problem:
$$
|\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -7 & 10 \\ -9 & -1 & -6 & 9 \\ -2 & 2 & 2 & -6 \\ 2 & 1 & 4 & -7\end{aligned}|
$$

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

*Hint: Use elementary column operations to make the entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{32}$ equal to zero.*
content.worked_solution:
Let's make entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{32}=2$ equal to zero using elementary column operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -7 & 10 \\ -9 & -1 & -6 & 9 \\ -2 & 2 & 2 & -6 \\ 2 & 1 & 4 & -7\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}+{C}_{2} \\ {C}_{3}:={C}_{3}+(-1){C}_{2} \\ {C}_{4}:={C}_{4}+3{C}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 & -5 & 4 \\ -10 & -1 & -5 & 6 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & 1 & 3 & -4\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $3$rd row, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 & -5 & 4 \\ -10 & -1 & -5 & 6 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & 1 & 3 & -4\end{aligned}| \\  & =2\cdot (-1)^{3+2}|\begin{aligned}-1 & -5 & 4 \\ -10 & -5 & 6 \\ 3 & 3 & -4\end{aligned}| \\  & =-2|\begin{aligned}-1 & -5 & 4 \\ -10 & -5 & 6 \\ 3 & 3 & -4\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Apply C1 ← C1 + 2C4, C2 ← C2 − 3C4, and C3 ← C3 + C4. These preserve the determinant and make row 1 equal to (0,0,0,3). Deleting row 1 and column 4 gives rows (4,−7,6), (−9,4,−6), and (11,−5,1). Expansion along row 1 has factor 3(−1)^(1+4)=−3, giving option d.

after.name: Question 8
after.problem:
$$
|\begin{aligned}-6 & 9 & -3 & 3 \\ 2 & -4 & 5 & 1 \\ -3 & -5 & -3 & -3 \\ 1 & 10 & -4 & 5\end{aligned}|
$$

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

*Hint: Use elementary column operations to make the entries to the left of ${a}_{14}$ equal to zero.*
after.worked_solution:
Let's make entries to the left of ${a}_{14}=3$ equal to zero using elementary column operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}-6 & 9 & -3 & 3 \\ 2 & -4 & 5 & 1 \\ -3 & -5 & -3 & -3 \\ 1 & 10 & -4 & 5\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}+2{C}_{4} \\ {C}_{2}:={C}_{2}+(-3){C}_{4} \\ {C}_{3}:={C}_{3}+{C}_{4}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 & 3 \\ 4 & -7 & 6 & 1 \\ -9 & 4 & -6 & -3 \\ 11 & -5 & 1 & 5\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $1$st row, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 & 3 \\ 4 & -7 & 6 & 1 \\ -9 & 4 & -6 & -3 \\ 11 & -5 & 1 & 5\end{aligned}| \\  & =3\cdot (-1)^{1+4}|\begin{aligned}4 & -7 & 6 \\ -9 & 4 & -6 \\ 11 & -5 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =-3|\begin{aligned}4 & -7 & 6 \\ -9 & 4 & -6 \\ 11 & -5 & 1\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Reducing a 4x4 Determinant to a 3x3 Determinant Using Column Operations
content.problem:
$$
|\begin{aligned}-6 & 9 & -3 & 3 \\ 2 & -4 & 5 & 1 \\ -3 & -5 & -3 & -3 \\ 1 & 10 & -4 & 5\end{aligned}|
$$

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

*Hint: Use elementary column operations to make the entries to the left of ${a}_{14}$ equal to zero.*
content.worked_solution:
Let's make entries to the left of ${a}_{14}=3$ equal to zero using elementary column operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}-6 & 9 & -3 & 3 \\ 2 & -4 & 5 & 1 \\ -3 & -5 & -3 & -3 \\ 1 & 10 & -4 & 5\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}+2{C}_{4} \\ {C}_{2}:={C}_{2}+(-3){C}_{4} \\ {C}_{3}:={C}_{3}+{C}_{4}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 & 3 \\ 4 & -7 & 6 & 1 \\ -9 & 4 & -6 & -3 \\ 11 & -5 & 1 & 5\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $1$st row, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 & 3 \\ 4 & -7 & 6 & 1 \\ -9 & 4 & -6 & -3 \\ 11 & -5 & 1 & 5\end{aligned}| \\  & =3\cdot (-1)^{1+4}|\begin{aligned}4 & -7 & 6 \\ -9 & 4 & -6 \\ 11 & -5 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =-3|\begin{aligned}4 & -7 & 6 \\ -9 & 4 & -6 \\ 11 & -5 & 1\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Hint: Use elementary column operations to make the entries to the left and to the right of a42 equal to zero.

decision.explanation: Apply C1 ← C1 + C2, C3 ← C3 − 2C2, and C4 ← C4 + 3C2. These preserve the determinant and make row 4 equal to (0,1,0,0). Expanding along row 4 gives the minor with rows (5,−3,7), (0,0,2), and (1,5,−5), with factor 1·(−1)^(4+2)=1. This is option e.

after.name: Question 9
after.problem:
$$
|\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & 1 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & 2 & -1 \\ 2 & -1 & 3 & -2 \\ -1 & 1 & 2 & -3\end{aligned}|
$$

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

*Hint: Use elementary column operations to make the entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{42}$ equal to zero.*
after.worked_solution:
Let's make entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{42}=1$ equal to zero using elementary column operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & 1 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & 2 & -1 \\ 2 & -1 & 3 & -2 \\ -1 & 1 & 2 & -3\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}+{C}_{2} \\ {C}_{3}:={C}_{3}+(-2){C}_{2} \\ {C}_{4}:={C}_{4}+3{C}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}5 & 2 & -3 & 7 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 2 \\ 1 & -1 & 5 & -5 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $4$th row, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}5 & 2 & -3 & 7 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 2 \\ 1 & -1 & 5 & -5 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot (-1)^{4+2}|\begin{aligned}5 & -3 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 \\ 1 & 5 & -5\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}5 & -3 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 \\ 1 & 5 & -5\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Reducing a 4x4 Determinant to a 3x3 Determinant Using Column Operations
content.problem:
$$
|\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & 1 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & 2 & -1 \\ 2 & -1 & 3 & -2 \\ -1 & 1 & 2 & -3\end{aligned}|
$$

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

*Hint: Use elementary column operations to make the entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{42}$ equal to zero.*
content.worked_solution:
Let's make entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{42}=1$ equal to zero using elementary column operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & 1 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & 2 & -1 \\ 2 & -1 & 3 & -2 \\ -1 & 1 & 2 & -3\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}+{C}_{2} \\ {C}_{3}:={C}_{3}+(-2){C}_{2} \\ {C}_{4}:={C}_{4}+3{C}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}5 & 2 & -3 & 7 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 2 \\ 1 & -1 & 5 & -5 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $4$th row, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}5 & 2 & -3 & 7 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 2 \\ 1 & -1 & 5 & -5 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot (-1)^{4+2}|\begin{aligned}5 & -3 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 \\ 1 & 5 & -5\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}5 & -3 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 \\ 1 & 5 & -5\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Apply C1 ← C1 + 2C2, C3 ← C3 + 3C2, and C4 ← C4 − 4C2. These preserve the determinant and make row 2 equal to (0,1,0,0). Expansion along row 2 gives the minor with rows (−3,−7,5), (5,10,−10), and (−2,−4,13). The cofactor factor is 1·(−1)^(2+2)=1, so option d has the same value.

after.name: Question 10
after.problem:
$$
|\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 & -4 & 1 \\ -2 & 1 & -3 & 4 \\ 1 & 2 & 4 & -2 \\ 2 & -2 & 2 & 5\end{aligned}|
$$

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

*Hint: Use elementary column operations to make the entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{22}$ equal to zero.*
after.worked_solution:
Let's make entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{22}=1$ equal to zero using elementary column operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 & -4 & 1 \\ -2 & 1 & -3 & 4 \\ 1 & 2 & 4 & -2 \\ 2 & -2 & 2 & 5\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}+2{C}_{2} \\ {C}_{3}:={C}_{3}+3{C}_{2} \\ {C}_{4}:={C}_{4}+(-4){C}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-3 & -1 & -7 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 5 & 2 & 10 & -10 \\ -2 & -2 & -4 & 13\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $2$nd row, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}-3 & -1 & -7 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 5 & 2 & 10 & -10 \\ -2 & -2 & -4 & 13\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot (-1)^{2+2}|\begin{aligned}-3 & -7 & 5 \\ 5 & 10 & -10 \\ -2 & -4 & 13\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-3 & -7 & 5 \\ 5 & 10 & -10 \\ -2 & -4 & 13\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

|\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 & -4 & 1 \\ -2 & 1 & -3 & 4 \\ 1 & 2 & 4 & -2 \\ 2 & -2 & 2 & 5\end{aligned}|

content.knowledge_point: Computing 4x4 Determinants Using Row and Column Operations
content.problem:
Calculate the value of 
$\,|\begin{aligned}3 & 9 & -6 & -3 \\ -5 & -6 & 10 & 12 \\ 2 & 2 & -1 & -1 \\ 4 & 8 & -8 & -2\end{aligned}|.$

*Hint: Use elementary column operations to make the entries to the right of ${a}_{11}$ equal to zero. You should be able to reduce the given $4\times 4$ determinant to a $3\times 3$ determinant.*
content.worked_solution:
Using elementary column operations, let's make entries to the right of ${a}_{11}=3$ equal to zero.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}3 & 9 & -6 & -3 \\ -5 & -6 & 10 & 12 \\ 2 & 2 & -1 & -1 \\ 4 & 8 & -8 & -2\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{2}:={C}_{2}+(-3){C}_{1} \\ {C}_{3}:={C}_{3}+2{C}_{1} \\ {C}_{4}:={C}_{4}+{C}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -5 & 9 & 0 & 7 \\ 2 & -4 & 3 & 1 \\ 4 & -4 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $1$st row, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -5 & 9 & 0 & 7 \\ 2 & -4 & 3 & 1 \\ 4 & -4 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =3\cdot (-1)^{1+1}|\begin{aligned}9 & 0 & 7 \\ -4 & 3 & 1 \\ -4 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =3\cdot |\begin{aligned}9 & 0 & 7 \\ -4 & 3 & 1 \\ -4 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =3\cdot (3)\cdot (-1)^{2+2}|\begin{aligned}9 & 7 \\ -4 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =9(18+28) \\  & =9(46) \\  & =414.\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Apply C2 ← C2 − 2C1, C3 ← C3 − 3C1, and C4 ← C4 + 2C1. These preserve the determinant and make row 2 equal to (1,0,0,0). Expansion along row 2 gives minus the determinant with rows (1,−2,1), (0,−2,0), and (5,4,−6). Its value is (−2)(−6−5)=22, so the original determinant is −22.

after.worked_solution:
Using elementary column operations, let's make entries to the right of ${a}_{21}=1$ equal to zero.

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 2 & 3 & -2 \\ 2 & 4 & 4 & -4 \\ -2 & 1 & -2 & -2\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{2}:={C}_{2}+(-2){C}_{1} \\ {C}_{3}:={C}_{3}+(-3){C}_{1} \\ {C}_{4}:={C}_{4}+2{C}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -2 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 0 & -2 & 0 \\ -2 & 5 & 4 & -6\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -2 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 0 & -2 & 0 \\ -2 & 5 & 4 & -6\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot (-1)^{2+1}|\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & -2 & 0 \\ 5 & 4 & -6\end{aligned}| \\  & =-|\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & -2 & 0 \\ 5 & 4 & -6\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-1)\cdot (-2)\cdot (-1)^{2+2}|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 5 & -6\end{aligned}| \\  & =2(-6-5) \\  & =-22.\end{aligned}

Hint: Use elementary row operations to make the entries above and below a32 equal to zero. You should be able to reduce the given 4×4 determinant to a 3×3 determinant.

a

decision.explanation: Apply R1 ← R1 + 2R3, R2 ← R2 + R3, and R4 ← R4 − R3. These preserve the determinant and make column 2 equal to (0,0,3,0). Expanding along column 2 gives −3 times the minor with rows (−3,−4,8), (0,6,−3), and (0,2,5). Thus the determinant is (−3)(−3)(6·5−(−3)·2)=9·36=324.

after.name: Question 14
after.problem:
Calculate the value of 
$\,|\begin{aligned}1 & -6 & -2 & 4 \\ 2 & -3 & 7 & -5 \\ -2 & 3 & -1 & 2 \\ -2 & 3 & 1 & 7\end{aligned}|.$

*Hint: Use elementary row operations to make the entries above and below ${a}_{32}$ equal to zero. You should be able to reduce the given $4\times 4$ determinant to a $3\times 3$ determinant.*
after.worked_solution:
Using elementary row operations, let's make entries above and below ${a}_{32}=3$ equal to zero.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & -6 & -2 & 4 \\ 2 & -3 & 7 & -5 \\ -2 & 3 & -1 & 2 \\ -2 & 3 & 1 & 7\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+2{R}_{3} \\ {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+{R}_{3} \\ {R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+(-1){R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 & -4 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 6 & -3 \\ -2 & 3 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 5\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $2$nd column, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 & -4 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 6 & -3 \\ -2 & 3 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 5\end{aligned}| \\  & =3\cdot (-1)^{3+2}|\begin{aligned}-3 & -4 & 8 \\ 0 & 6 & -3 \\ 0 & 2 & 5\end{aligned}| \\  & =-3|\begin{aligned}-3 & -4 & 8 \\ 0 & 6 & -3 \\ 0 & 2 & 5\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-3)\cdot -3\cdot (-1)^{1+1}|\begin{aligned}6 & -3 \\ 2 & 5\end{aligned}| \\  & =9(30+6) \\  & =324.\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
Using elementary row operations, let's make entries below ${a}_{12}=1$ equal to zero.

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 & 4 & 3 \\ 2 & -2 & -8 & -1 \\ -3 & 3 & 7 & 5 \\ -4 & -1 & -4 & -1\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-3){R}_{1} \\ {R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 & 4 & 3 \\ -4 & 0 & 0 & 5 \\ 6 & 0 & -5 & -4 \\ -7 & 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 & 4 & 3 \\ -4 & 0 & 0 & 5 \\ 6 & 0 & -5 & -4 \\ -7 & 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot (-1)^{1+2}|\begin{aligned}-4 & 0 & 5 \\ 6 & -5 & -4 \\ -7 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =-|\begin{aligned}-4 & 0 & 5 \\ 6 & -5 & -4 \\ -7 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-1)\cdot -5\cdot (-1)^{2+2}|\begin{aligned}-4 & 5 \\ -7 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =5(-8+35) \\  & =135.\end{aligned}
